references.text: Balaam again tells the messengers to stay overnight while he waits for a word from the Lord, following the same pattern as in verse 8.
God reveals Himself to prophets through visions and dreams, which is what Balaam expects when he asks them to wait overnight.
God speaks to Laban in a dream at night, an example of how God communicates with people during the night.
God came to Abimelech in a dream at night, similar to the way Balaam expects to receive God's word.
Jeremiah waits to hear what the Lord will answer, paralleling Balaam's waiting for the Lord's word.
The prophet Habakkuk waits to see what God will speak to him, similar to Balaam's attitude.
Peter mentions Balaam as an example of someone who sought profit through his prophetic gift.
